fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly on both sides to guide first-arriving units directly to the access point without hesitation.
• Post a visible site map near the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the garage, and the equipment storage area so responders can orient quickly on arrival.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a driveway width adequate for emergency vehicles.
• Trim tree branches overhanging the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for ladder trucks and other tall emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation that reduces sight lines along the access drive, particularly on curves or rises created by the steep terrain.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point on the property that can accommodate a fire engine or ambulance, and keep that area clear of parked vehicles and stored equipment.
• Keep the equipment storage area clear of the access drive so emergency vehicles are not blocked from reaching the rear of the property.
• Number or label each detached structure visibly from the access drive so responders can identify and communicate about individual buildings during an incident.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and each detached structure so responders can move on foot between buildings without pushing through vegetation.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure on all sides.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest the structure to create open gaps between the canopy and the roofline.
• Remove woody debris piled or scattered near the structure and any outbuildings.
• Cut back or mow grass cover surrounding the structure, keeping it short during dry periods.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back shrubs growing along the driveway edges that have narrowed the travel lane.
• Thin scattered trees along the driveway to maintain a clear path for emergency vehicles.
• Separate vegetation from the structure on the rear side to allow movement and access around the back of the building.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from shrub bases near the structure.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure clear of loose plant material, cut brush, and dry grass clippings.
• Thin scattered shrubs in the open terrain nearest the structure to reduce the amount of vegetation feeding a fire moving toward the house.
